problem.text: HumanEval previously requested automatic BOS insertion for every prompt format, including Gemma's template, which already begins with <bos>.

reasoning.text: The change moves BOS selection into model-specific prompt text rather than applying one tokenizer-level policy to all formats.

impact.text: Automatic BOS insertion remains enabled only for explicit --prompt_format raw. Omitting the option selects the separate unwrapped-completion path and now disables automatic BOS insertion.

source_notes.text: The parent entry describes the earlier Qwen3 preset integration with BOS still requested during encoding.

Closed issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” concerns conversion and tokenizer truncation, not HumanEval BOS placement; it supplies no direct validation of this change.

limitations: No real tokenizer, model generation or HumanEval scoring was executed. Recognition of each literal marker depends on the selected tokenizer.
The bounded Python check models template edits and flag selection; it does not establish token IDs, token counts or score improvements.

claims.text: The templates gain these leading markers: granite and reka use <|endoftext|>; llama and mistral use <s>; llama3 uses <|begin_of_text|>; deepseek uses <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>. Gemma retains its existing <bos>, while chatml and qwen3 gain no BOS text.

main substitutes the problem into the selected template, encodes it once, and passes the resulting input_ids to each sample Job. Special-token encoding stays enabled. Tokenizer.encode routes this through encode_special, whose underlying tokenizer call disables automatic special-token addition; the wrapper independently prepends bos_token_id only when add_bos is true and that ID exists.

This removes the extra wrapper-inserted BOS from Gemma and avoids imposing one on ChatML/Qwen3. For the six newly prefixed templates, preservation of the old token sequence depends on the literal marker encoding to the same configured BOS ID; source inspection alone cannot establish that equivalence.

A standard-library check extracted the parent templates and modeled the patch: all problem-placeholder counts were preserved, and only explicit raw retained automatic BOS. The no-option path remained distinct from raw.

annotation.summary: Makes HumanEval BOS handling template-specific, retaining automatic insertion only for explicit raw mode.

argv:
import ast,json
from pathlib import Path
t=ast.parse(Path('eval/humaneval.py').read_text())
p=next(ast.literal_eval(n.value) for n in t.body if isinstance(n,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(x,ast.Name) and x.id=='prompt_formats' for x in n.targets))
add={'granite':'<|endoftext|>','llama':'<s>','llama3':'<|begin_of_text|>','mistral':'<s>','reka':'<|endoftext|>','deepseek':'<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>'}
for k in [None,*p]:
 old='{{problem}}' if k is None else p[k][0]
 new=add.get(k,'')+old
 print(json.dumps({'format':k,'automatic_bos_before':True,'automatic_bos_after':k=='raw','added_text':add.get(k,''),'problem_slots_preserved':old.count('{{problem}}')==new.count('{{problem}}')},ensure_ascii=False))
